lines: כִּי לֵב טָהוֹר בְּךָ, הוֹי מַחְסִי

review: The refrain is the Arabic's bracketed (فِي انْتِظَارِكَ أَبِي)3 — printed once with a repetition mark. The payload keeps it once per stanza, because the reader prints one line and the threefold repetition is a musical direction, not three lines of text.
1:1–3 the anaphora בְּצִפִּיָּה is kept on every line, as the Arabic repeats فِي انْتِظَارِ four times per stanza; the opening word is the stanza's shape, so it is never varied for metre.

2:2 כִּלְיוֹתַי — the Arabic مَا يُضْنِي حَشَايَ is 'what wastes my inward parts'; the Hebrew keeps the psalm's כִּלְיוֹת (Ps 73:21, Job 19:27) rather than a flat 'my inside', so the complaint has a body.
2:3 לֵב טָהוֹר … מַחְסִי — Ps 51:12 (לֵב טָהוֹר בְּרָא־לִי) with Ps 62:8 (מַחְסִי); the Arabic نَقَاءُ الْقَلْبِ فِيكَ يَا حِمَايَ pairs cleanness with shelter, and the Hebrew keeps both nouns.

4:1–2 the prayer is made 'in the name of the beloved Lord' and answered 'in His name', keeping the two prepositions of the Arabic (بِاسْمِ الْحَبِيبِ … بِاسْمِهِ) rather than merging them into one mention of the name.
